data.title: 25 New York restaurants worth planning around
data.seoTitle: 25 Best Restaurants in New York City
data.seoDescription: Explore 25 New York restaurants for memorable dinners, casual slices, neighborhood institutions and destination meals across Manhattan and Brooklyn.
data.summary: A wide-ranging New York restaurant shortlist, from defining neighborhood institutions to dining rooms worth booking a trip around.
data.body: This guide balances destination restaurants with casual places that reveal how New York actually eats. The order favors memorable food, a useful range of neighborhoods and different reasons to go, from an easy slice to a dinner worth planning around. Reservations, menus and hours can change quickly, so confirm directly with each restaurant.

items.name: Tatiana by Kwame Onwuachi
items.description: A celebratory dining room at Lincoln Center where Caribbean, West African and New York influences meet in generous, high-energy dishes.

items.name: Semma
items.description: Regional South Indian cooking with deep spice, seafood and dishes that move well beyond the usual restaurant canon.

items.name: Torrisi
items.description: An exuberant Italian American dining room with polished service and a menu shaped by downtown New York.

items.name: Don Angie
items.description: Inventive Italian American plates in an intimate room where the lasagna and shareable pastas reward planning ahead.

items.name: Via Carota
items.description: A warm neighborhood trattoria known for vegetables, handmade pastas and an atmosphere that works from late lunch through dinner.

items.name: Dhamaka
items.description: Bold regional Indian cooking with offal, slow-cooked meats and dishes rarely represented on New York menus.

items.name: COTE Korean Steakhouse
items.description: Korean barbecue technique and steakhouse sourcing come together in a polished, social format built for a group.

items.name: 4 Charles Prime Rib
items.description: A small, clubby steakhouse where prime rib, burgers and classic sides make the reservation part of the experience.

items.name: Atomix
items.description: A tasting-menu experience that presents modern Korean cooking through precise courses, ceramics and thoughtful storytelling.

items.name: Fish Cheeks
items.description: Bright, family-style Thai seafood with curries, whole fish and enough contrast to make ordering widely the best approach.

items.name: Thai Diner
items.description: Thai comfort food, playful diner references and a welcoming all-day room make this an easy downtown anchor.

items.name: Shukette
items.description: Open-fire cooking, breads and eastern Mediterranean small plates create a loud, communal dinner with plenty to pass around.

items.name: Golden Diner
items.description: A compact diner that filters New York classics through Korean American flavors without losing the comfort of the originals.

items.name: Dame
items.description: A small seafood restaurant with a focused menu, excellent fish and chips and the energy of a neighborhood favorite.

items.name: Lilia
items.description: Wood-fired seafood, handmade pasta and a converted Williamsburg garage combine for a quintessential Brooklyn dinner.

items.name: Misi
items.description: A focused menu of vegetables and handmade pastas served in a spare waterfront room with a clear point of view.

items.name: Lucali
items.description: Candlelit Brooklyn pizza with a concise menu and a famously patient wait; arrive with time and a flexible evening.

items.name: L’Industrie Pizzeria
items.description: Crisp, expressive slices finished with high-quality toppings make this a strong stop without committing to a full dinner.

items.name: Scarr’s Pizza
items.description: A downtown slice shop with house-milled flour, a retro room and pizza that balances nostalgia with real craft.

items.name: Los Tacos No. 1
items.description: Fast-moving counters turn out adobada, carne asada and nopal tacos that fit easily into a day of exploring.

items.name: Katz’s Delicatessen
items.description: The city’s best-known delicatessen remains worth understanding on its own terms: hand-carved pastrami, a ticket system and serious portions.

items.name: Russ & Daughters Cafe
items.description: A sit-down expression of the appetizing tradition, with smoked fish, bagels, eggs and classic Lower East Side flavors.

items.name: Sylvia’s
items.description: A Harlem landmark for fried chicken, ribs, greens and the history of a family-run restaurant woven into its neighborhood.

items.name: Sofreh
items.description: Persian cooking centered on herbs, rice, bread and slow-building flavors in a calm Brooklyn dining room.

items.name: Eyval
items.description: Contemporary Iranian cooking uses smoke, charcoal and bright herbs in a menu designed for sharing across the table.

places.name: Ayah Restaurant
places.description: Ayah Restaurant is described as the prettiest new Moroccan restaurant in NYC, located in SoHo. It features beautiful Marrakesh-inspired interiors with hanging lamps, painted ceilings, and textiles. The restaurant is buzzy with a stylish crowd, offering an interesting food menu, delicious pistachio crème brûlée, and Moroccan tea. Live music and dancing take place on some nights. It's recommended for groups, though tables for two or four are close together.

places.name: Jase's BBQ
places.description: Trinidadian-inspired BBQ stall featuring Caribbean flavors, perfectly smoked meats, and passion fruit BBQ sauce.
places.address: Time Out Market, Union Square, NYC

places.name: Nothing Really Matters
places.description: A super cool speakeasy hidden inside the 50th Street 1 train station on the Downtown side that serves amazing cocktails and pizza. Perfect for a pre-show drink or quick food.
